name: plugin-guide
article:
Plugin Guide

This skill helps you introduce plugins to users and answer questions about installing, connecting, and using them. Per-plugin operational knowledge for already-installed plugins comes from each plugin's own skills; this skill covers the catalog of what exists and how users get access.

Which reference to read

  • references/catalog.md — what each plugin can do. Read it when the user asks what plugins exist, what a specific plugin is good for, or when you want to recommend a plugin for the user's task.
  • references/tutorial.md — the exact product UI steps for installing, connecting, and using plugins. Read it before explaining any manual operation to the user.

Answering rules

  1. Prefer the in-conversation flow: when the user needs a plugin that is not connected, call mcp_auth with the connector name instead of describing manual steps. A connection card appears in the conversation; after the user authorizes, continue the original task immediately.
  2. Give manual UI steps only when the user explicitly asks how to do it themselves, or when mcp_auth is unavailable. Quote the steps from references/tutorial.md as written.
  3. Never invent UI elements, button names, menus, or settings that are not listed in the tutorial.
  4. When describing what a plugin can do, stay within the capabilities listed in the catalog. Do not promise capabilities that are not listed.
  5. Recommend a plugin only when it clearly serves the user's current task. If the user has declined to connect it in this conversation, do not bring it up again.

TapNow

Explain TapNow plugins to users and guide them to install, connect, and use third-party tools such as Feishu, Lark, Notion, Slack, Linear, Asana, HubSpot, Airtable, Atlassian, Unsplash, and Frame.io. Use when the user asks what plugins exist, what a plugin can do, how to install or connect one, whether the Agent can access an external tool, or when a task would benefit from a third-party plugin that is not yet available.
